body:
Is this not guaranteed to be true by the check above:
```cpp
if (autosmooth && smoothing_angle > 0.1) {
```
Should that check have been just:
```cpp
if (autosmooth) {
```
See my question if that original branching was a bug or intended. I would need to fix that depending on what it was.

My suspicion would be that the else branch should have been after `if (smoothing_angle > 0.1) {` not after `if (autosmooth) {`, it makes more sense (i.e. the check outside should just be `if (autosmooth) {`
Remove the` smoothing_angle > 0.1` check from the `if (autosmooth && smoothing_angle > 0.1) {` check because the intention was likely to run with the default normal when we are below that angle.

Sorry I haven't had time lately.
If this is what I think it is, when `Autosmooth` is enabled but angle is below `0.1`, it should disable smoothing altogether, not use the default, so all faces would be flat and we skip the calculations.
I will try to answer the other posts when I get some time.

Edit: Since you are doing the old smooth calculation in a separate function, feel free to delete the `else` branch, as it's supposed to be doing the same thing.
